title: 1989 AHSME Problem 4
statement: In the figure, \(ABCD\) is an isosceles trapezoid with side lengths \(AD=BC=5,\) \(AB=4,\) and \(DC=10.\) The point \(C\) is on \(\overline{DF}\) and \(B\) is the midpoint of hypotenuse \(\overline{DE}\) in the right triangle \(DEF.\) Then \(CF=\)

solutions.text:
Drop perpendiculars \(AG\) and \(BH\) to \(DF.\) In the isosceles trapezoid, \(GH=AB=4\) and \[ DG=HC=\frac{DC-AB}{2}=3. \] Since \(B\) is the midpoint of \(DE\) and \(BH\parallel EF,\) the midpoint theorem makes \(H\) the midpoint of \(DF.\) Hence \(DH=DG+GH=7,\) so \(DF=14\) and \(CF=14-10=4.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: The segment through midpoint \(B\) parallel to \(EF\) reaches the midpoint of \(DF\)
